notes: Attribute-metric charter: the primary metric is a proportion (defective orders / orders presented), stated as a 0-1 proportion in the metric fields so every downstream tool -- p-chart, proportion tests, gap arithmetic -- carries the same unit. The 8.6% magnitude is the Q2 2026 reject-log rate; Measure's job is to put a real baseline window and measurement check under it. Business impact is the COPQ worksheet's engine total x 4, one number, one source.

problem_statement.what: Finished print orders are failing the customer's first-presentation check -- wrong paper stock, crooked trim, ink smudge or banding, or wrong quantity -- and going back for reprint
problem_statement.where: Campus print shop, main production room, both shifts (day and evening)
problem_statement.when: Q2 2026 (April-June), still running at the same level in late June

magnitude.unit: % of orders rejected at first presentation

goal.statement: Cut the first-presentation defect rate from 0.086 (Q2 2026 reject log) to 0.043 -- half -- by 2026-09-30, measured at the QC desk as the proportion of orders rejected at any of the four named checks, while holding turnaround and press overtime.

scope.in_scope: Produced print orders handed off at the QC desk: course packets, flyers and posters, programs and booklets, and counter jobs, both shifts, Monday-Saturday.
scope.out_scope: Self-serve copier output, mail-room work, jobs brokered to the off-campus vendor, pricing and billing disputes, and the online ordering portal's usability.

team.name: Tessa Nguyen
team.role: Day-shift lead, QC desk -- process owner

team.name: Jordan Pike
team.role: Student staff, intake desk and prepress

timeline.name: Measurement check passed, collection plan live

business_impact.basis: COPQ worksheet print-copq: Q2 2026 engine total $5,930.15 x 4 quarters

risks.risk: Fall term starts 2026-08-31: order volume and rush share surge in the final weeks of the project window, which could raise the defect rate and mask a real improvement
risks.mitigation: Record daily order counts and order type all window; state the surge on any before/after claim; compare like-for-like weeks where possible

risks.risk: Student staff turnover at term start -- new hands at intake and finishing raise error rates
risks.mitigation: Keep the four checks and any changed method written at the workstation, step by step, so the standard does not live in one person's head

risks.risk: Defect judgments drift between raters -- 'smudge' and 'acceptable ink variation' called differently by different people makes the rate move without the process moving
risks.mitigation: Two-rater agreement check (T-12) before the baseline window opens; re-run after any definition change
